newsitem.title: GERMANY: New Ukraine currency not a panacea - Deutsche Bank.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine currency not a panacea - Deutsche Bank.

text.p: Ukraine's decision to launch a new currency next week will not solve all the nation's problems and more work lies ahead on monetary and fiscal policies, Deutsche Bank Research said on Wednesday.

"Trust in a new currency can only be maintained if the reforms in Kiev gain momentum. Especially fiscal and monetary problems must be solved and structural changes must continue," the group's analysts wrote in a report on Ukraine. One hryvna will be worth 100,000 karbovanets, also known as "coupons."
Ukraine will introduce a new currency, the hryvna, from September 2 and the new notes will will be exchanged for the existing karbovanets currency between September 2 and 16.
The new currency will knock five zeroes off the former Soviet republic's unwieldy inflation-hit prices.
Deutsche said more action needed to be taken on sorting out domestic political conflicts and reducing the state's role in the economy.
"Positive growth is not yet in sight in statistics, but the shadow economy is booming. The government tends to direct intervention instead of letting market forces guide the economy," the bank said.

After the exchange, the hryvna would be stabilized at around 1.75 to 1.76 to the dollar, deputy prime minister Viktor Pynzenyk said at the weekend. That is close to the equivalent karbovanets rate on Sunday of 180,000 per dollar.
